doc.title: Jane Bunnett interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 25, 2024

title: Record display, Slim Gaillard, Hermeto Pascoal and Don Pullen's solo record
summary: Looking at her display, she recalls Slim Gaillard living with them four years, working with Hermeto Pascoal, Jon Hendricks, Stanley Cowell, and Don Pullen's 1975 solo record.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Yeah also, you can’t see it but on the wall in front of me I have four pages of information about you including your awards and nominations, and the fact that you can share a record display with your band on top of Duke Ellington and just down the road from Art Tatum.
I know. Isn’t that sort of self-gratification. It is. I got this. And then I’ve got some of the great people that —
So Slim lived off and on with us for four years.

Oh my God. What an incredible whacky time that was. And then we got to work with the great Hermeto Pascoal. Had a big concert here with him. And Jon Hendricks — did some shows with Jon Hendricks here. Of course Stanley Cowell, one of my heroes. Stanley Cowell, made a beautiful, beautiful record. And this was one of the most inspiring records for me, that was Don Pullen’s solo record. That was sort of in between — that was done in 1975. Wow. © Fillius Jazz Archive -17-
